prompt.brief: Design a resumable migration platform that transfers petabytes of data to Google Cloud, validates integrity and permissions, and minimizes application downtime during cutover.
successSignals: Treat source snapshots, change logs, checksums, and destination manifests as explicit migration phases with durable checkpoints.
Copy files and database ranges in parallel, validate samples and full checksums, then drain changes before a reversible cutover.
Protect source production traffic with bandwidth and read quotas and encrypt data in transit and at rest.
Explain schema mapping, duplicate files, changed rows, failed chunks, rollback, retention, and audit evidence.

functional: Inventory sources, define destination mappings, transfer files and database partitions, and maintain incremental change capture.
Expose per-object or per-range progress, checksum results, lag, throughput, validation failures, and cutover readiness.
Support pause/resume, re-copy, schema transformation, access-policy mapping, final freeze, promotion, and rollback.
nonFunctional: Keep the final freeze and cutover within the agreed downtime window while bulk transfer runs for weeks beforehand.
Transfer petabytes through partitioned resumable workers without saturating source systems or one hot prefix.
Make chunks, change-log positions, validation reports, and promotion steps idempotent and auditable.
Pause safely on source or destination faults and resume from checkpoints without skipping changed data.
scaleAssumptions: Migrate multiple petabytes of objects and tens of terabytes of databases across a multi-month program.
Partition objects by prefix and databases by table or key range; isolate high-write tables and large files.
Retain manifests, change logs, checksums, access mappings, and cutover evidence for replay and audit.

metrics.label: Migration volume
metrics.description: Volume drives chunking, bandwidth limits, lifecycle tiers, and validation design.

metrics.label: Cutover downtime
metrics.description: Bulk copy is asynchronous; only final change drain and promotion affect application availability.

metrics.label: Durable boundary
metrics.description: The source remains authoritative until validated destination manifests are promoted atomically.

metrics.label: Async boundary
metrics.description: Keep bulk copying, checksum validation, reconciliation, and reporting asynchronous.

dataFlow.title: Accept Migrate petabytes of data
dataFlow.description: The Resumable migration platform gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The migration control plane records a versioned plan, source snapshot, and idempotency key before transfer begins.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed Resumable migration platform events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.title: Build the read model
dataFlow.description: Partitioned workers consume Resumable migration platform events, update the serving projection, and expose lag or watermark metadata.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the Resumable migration platform projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Resumable migration platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Resumable migration platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Resumable migration platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Resumable migration platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Resumable migration platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Resumable migration platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Resumable migration platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Resumable migration platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Resumable migration platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines inventory, transfer, validation, cutover, rollback, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and source/chunk/table keys support transfer, validation, cutover, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Resumable migration platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
